title: Tip Calculator
story: Dinner was $87.50. Service was excellent — 20% tip. Split between 3 people. What does each person owe? Mental math at the table is error-prone. Build a tip calculator that handles any bill, any percentage, any number of people — the most practical program you'll write this week.
why: A tip calculator teaches percentage arithmetic, splitting/rounding, and producing clear formatted output — immediate real-world utility.
analogy: A restaurant bill with a scribbled tip calculation on the back of a napkin: '87.50 × 0.20 = 17.50, total = 105.00, ÷ 3 = 35 each.' Your tip calculator does it instantly, with a breakdown of different percentages so you can pick based on service quality. The napkin, digitized.
try_it: Round up to the nearest dollar. Add service quality as input: Poor=10%, Good=15%, Great=20%, Amazing=25%. Show tip, total, and per-person amount for each quality level. Print a formatted 'receipt' with all calculations.
tips: Tip = bill × percentage / 100 — the fundamental formula
Always check for 0 people before dividing
Round UP for tips — being generous with rounding is appreciated
common_mistakes: Using float division and losing cents — work in cents (multiply by 100) for exact math
Dividing by 0 people — validate input before computing
Forgetting that tip percent is an integer (15, not 0.15) when doing bill * pct / 100
